newsitem.title: EGYPT: SOCCER-EGYPT CLUB SEEKS RECORD FOURTH AFRICA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EGYPT CLUB SEEKS RECORD FOURTH AFRICA CUP.

text.p: Zamalek captain Ismail Youssef chases a remarkable record in Cairo on Friday when he and his Egyptian club seek a record fourth African Champions Cup title in the second leg of the final against Shooting Stars of Nigeria.

The 32-year-old midfielder, who played for his country in the 1990 World Cup finals in Italy, will be hoping to lead the Cairo aristrocrats back from a 2-1 deficit after the first leg in Nigeria two weeks ago.
Youssef was just 20 when Zamalek won their first African Champions Cup title in 1984, beating Stars 2-0 on aggregate in the final.

He took a winners' medal again in 1986 and 1993 when Zamalek needed post-match penalty shootouts to win the continent's top club prize and is confident of a fourth as Zamalek seek to set a new winning record in the African Champions Cup.

"We will be pressing from the start. All the players want to score but we are also mindful of the counter-attack,'' Youssef said of the tactical approach the Nigerians are expected to take to defend their 2-1 aggregate lead.

Stars will be seeking to become the first Nigerian team to win the trophy and have delayed their arrival in the Egyptian capital until Thursday to avoid the intense pre-match pressure building up in Cairo.
Zamalek need just a 1-0 win to take the Cup on away goal rules and complete an Egyptian double after Arab Contractors' victory in last Friday's African Cup Winners' Cup final.
Utility player Tarek Mustapha, who scored the vital away goal in the final minute of the first leg in Ibadan, will be Zamalek's key after a meteoric rise in Egyptian football.

The 25-year-old, who recently won a first cap for the national team, was playing in the second division last season but is now the toast of Zamalek's fanatical fans. He says he prefers to play as an attacking midfielder but is encouraged to press forward by Zamalek's German coach Olk Werner.

Mustapha also says an expected capacity crowd of 80000 at the Cairo stadium will provide the necessary inspiration for more goals. "The crowd will also certainly kill the confidence of the Nigerians once they walk out on the pitch,'' he added.
Zamalek rounded off their preparations with a 4-0 league win over fifth-placed Gomhouriya Shebin on Saturday, including two goals from another key performer and World Cup veteran, Ahmed El Kass.
